## ACCEPT the measurement — and ⛔ **LEG 3 FIRED**, so the merge is the maintainer's ruling, not this seat's. PR stays DRAFT.

`domain:devx @ objectui` PM seat (`session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`), R55, 2026-09-12T21:3xZ. Head `ed8e1b1be4`, base `d7f0601ee7`. **Two files: `pnpm-lock.yaml` (+186 / −761) and one empty-frontmatter changeset.** ⛔ Nothing else in the diff — which was the whole point of B-before-A.

### Verified by this seat against the diff, ⛔ not taken from the report

| claim | re-derivation |
|:--|:--|
| dedicated PR, lockfile only | ✅ 2 files; **0 `package.json` changed** |
| identities 1814 → 1767 | ✅ `resolution:` lines 1814 → 1767 |
| ⭐ the identity-sensitive copies really disappear | ✅ `react-router@7.18.0` **2 → 0**, `react-router-dom@7.18.0` **2 → 0**, `motion@13.1.1` **2 → 0** |

⭐ **Every figure the card predicted reproduced exactly on today's tip, with nothing to explain** — and the committed lockfile's sha256 is still `e4e3a203f2…`, byte-identical to the card's reading four days ago, so the base itself never moved. ⚠️ That is a *lucky* outcome, not a reason to have skipped the re-derivation: triage said explicitly it had re-run none of it and that the registry had moved under objectui#8333's numbers in four days.

⭐ The control ran **both directions in the same run**: `pnpm install --lockfile-only` on the unmodified base reproduces the committed lockfile byte-identically (matching sha256, empty `git diff --stat`), **and** a strict one-byte append (701203 → 701204) makes the same command print `1 file changed`. ⇒ the empty reading is a measurement, ⛔ not a broken command. Restore proven by sha256 and an empty diff, ⛔ never by an exit code.

### ⛔⛔ LEG 3 FIRES — all eight identity-sensitive packages are hit

`react-router` 7.18.0→7.18.2 · `react-router-dom` 7.18.0→7.18.2 · the five `@radix-ui/react-{slot,primitive,id,compose-refs,use-layout-effect}` · `motion` 13.1.1→13.2.0.

⚠️ **And the round found a sharper point than triage's fence anticipated**: the collapse is **the OLDER of two versions being dropped and its consumers moving up** — ⛔ not two copies of one version merging. ⇒ for those consumers, **behaviour moves as well as bytes**, within range.

⇒ per triage's ruling — 「⇒ that reading is what turns this into a maintainer decision, and it belongs **on the PR with numbers attached**, ⛔ not asked in advance without them」 — this seat ⛔ does **not** flip ready, ⛔ does not enqueue, ⛔ does not arm auto-merge, and ⛔ does not rule the merge. Routed to the maintainer with the numbers attached, which is exactly the shape triage asked for.

### ⭐ The card's question 1 is ANSWERED: **accretion, not intent**

⛔ No declaration, range or override selects any dropped copy — verified structurally: `overrides:`, `settings:` and `patchedDependencies:` are byte-identical by sha256; inside `importers:` (2834 lines both sides) **0 `specifier:` lines change**, 114 `version:` lines change, 0 other lines change. The dropped copies come from third-party subtrees — `cmdk@1.1.1` for the radix five, `fumadocs-ui` for motion, `react-router-dom@7.18.0` for react-router — plus `packages/plugin-designer`'s peer range, **which does not even satisfy the repo's own `^7.18.2`**. And all 47 dropped versions have a strictly higher surviving sibling, so ⛔ nothing can move backward. `check-lockfile-integrity` agrees: `VERDICT clean — no @objectstack/* identity moved backward and no package gained a copy`.

### ⚠️ `Bundle Analysis` will be RED, and the red is NOT fixable in this PR

The aggregate **improves**: eager closure 3116.3 → 3105.3 KB (**−11.0 KB**), every per-chunk ceiling passes, entry chunk −65 raw / −16 gzip. Per chunk: `vendor-react` **−9.3 KB** (react-router collapsing), `vendor-markdown` −2.1, `vendor-radix` −1.0, `ui-components` **+1.7**.

What reds is the **ceiling-sensitivity leg on `ui-components`**: headroom 3.5 KB (0.04×) → 1.9 KB (0.02×, EXHAUSTED) against a declared 4289-byte allowance that reds below 3378. ⭐ The checker's own verdict text forbids both edits that would turn it green — ⛔ never raise the ceiling, ⛔ never raise the allowance — and says to take the row to its open card. ⇒ reported on **objectui#7848** (open, `pm:blocked`, `domain:devx`) as a measured data point, ⛔ nothing raised, ⛔ nothing re-pinned, ⛔ no new card filed because that row already has an owner.

⚠️ The round's own inference, stated **as** an inference: the `ui-components` chunk rule matches `packages/(components|fields)` source only, that source is byte-identical across both builds, so what moved is the bundler emitting their dists (`vite` 8.2.1→8.2.2 and `rolldown` 1.2.3→1.2.7 both collapse here). ⛔ Not pinned byte-by-byte, and labelled as such.

⇒ **`Bundle Analysis` is a required context**, so this PR cannot land on this seat's authority regardless of leg 3. Both questions go up together.

### ⭐ Two things this round refused, both correctly

1. ⛔ **No gate tracking the duplicate count over time** — triage fenced it as a different card, 「the count is not decidable as a threshold until this PR shows what the healthy number is」. ⭐ This run now shows it: **1773 resolutions / 1767 identities, with 45 names still carrying more than one copy after dedupe** (minimatch ×4, picomatch ×2, tinyexec ×2 among them) ⇒ a future threshold card now has a baseline, which is precisely what the fence was waiting for.
2. ⛔ **No new card for the `ui-components` red** — objectui#7848 already owns that number, named by the checker itself.

### ⇒ What this seat is doing, and what it is not

⛔ Not merging. ⛔ Not flipping ready. ⛔ Not arming. ⭐ Labelling `needs-user-decision`, requesting review, and handing the maintainer **two rulings with numbers attached** — the merge (leg 3), and how the `Bundle Analysis` red is handled at merge time. objectui#8333 stays `pm:blocked` on this card until the first is answered.
